extracted.intended_audience: applicants, intervenors, commenters, members of the public, Tribal governments, resource agencies, and regulated entities participating in FERC proceedings and respondents to FLRA OIG system-of-records notice
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content requirements for submitting scoping comments, interventions, protests, and related filings in FERC proceedings (and for submitting comments/responding to an FLRA OIG system-of-records notice). Includes deadlines, filing methods, service obligations, NEPA scoping expectations, and privacy/routine-use disclosures for investigative records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water quality certification filing requirement (60 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must file no later than 60 days following the date of issuance of this notice: (1) a copy of the water quality certification; (2) a copy of the request for certification, including proof of the date on which the certifying agency received the request; or (3) evidence of waiver of water quality certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit procedural requirement for applicants to document water quality certification status; filing must occur within 60 days of notice issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural schedule — comments and reply comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The application will be processed according to the following schedule. Filing of Comments, Recommendations, Terms and Conditions, and Prescriptions: July 12, 2025. Filing of Reply Comments: August 26, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates are target milestones; revisions to the schedule will be made as appropriate. Filings submitted after dates may be untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final amendments deadline (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final amendments to the application must be filed with the Commission no later than 30 days from the issuance date of this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure substantive changes are submitted within this 30-day window to be considered part of the application record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping comments deadline and rule on deadlines falling on weekends/holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for Filing Scoping Comments: on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on June 15, 2025. The Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure provide that if a deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, holiday, or other day when the Commission is closed for business, the deadline does not end until the close of business on the next business day. Because the 60‑day filing deadline falls on Sunday (i.e., June 15, 2025), the filing deadline is extended until on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Monday, June 16, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 18 CFR 385.2007(a)(2) for deadline extensions when deadlines fall on non-business days; confirm the extended due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing encouraged; eComment character limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission strongly encourages electronic filing. Use the Commission’s eFiling system at https://ferconline.ferc.gov/FERCOnline.aspx. Commenters can submit brief comments up to 6,000 characters, without prior registration, using the eComment system at https://ferconline.ferc.gov/QuickComment.aspx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use eFiling for full filings and eComment for short submissions (≤6,000 characters). Contact FERC Online Support for assistance; paper filings remain possible if electronic filing is infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper submission addresses and identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In lieu of electronic filing, you may submit a paper copy. Submissions sent via the U.S. Postal Service must be addressed to Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Room 1A, Washington, DC 20426. Submissions sent via any other carrier must be addressed to: Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 12225 Wilkins Avenue, Rockville, Maryland 20852. All filings must clearly identify the project name and docket number on the first page: Lake Algonquin Hydroelectric Project (P—7274—035).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing paper, ensure the first page clearly lists the project name and docket number to avoid misplacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for intervenors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s Rules of Practice require all intervenors filing documents with the Commission to serve a copy of that document on each person on the official service list for the project. Further, if an intervenor files comments or documents with the Commission relating to the merits of an issue that may affect the responsibilities of a particular resource agency, they must also serve a copy of the document on that resource agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervenors must confirm the official service list and serve all listed parties and any affected resource agencies when filings affect agency responsibilities; failure to serve can affect parties' rights and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application status — accepted but not ready for environmental analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: This application has been accepted for filing but is not ready for environmental analysis at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance for filing is procedural and does not imply environmental sufficiency; stakeholders should monitor further notices when the project is ready for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping process under NEPA — EA or EIS and solicitation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to NEPA, Commission staff intends to prepare either an environmental assessment (EA) or an environmental impact statement (EIS) that describes and evaluates the probable effects, including an assessment of the site-specific and cumulative effects, if any, of the proposed action and alternatives. The Commission’s scoping process will help determine the required level of analysis and satisfy the NEPA scoping requirements. The Commission is soliciting written comments and suggestions on the preliminary list of issues and alternatives to be addressed in the NEPA document, as described in scoping document 1 (SD1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should focus on issues and alternatives to be included in the NEPA document; staff may use scoping comments to decide whether an EA or EIS is required. There is currently no on-site scoping meeting anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing SD1 and application documents via eLibrary
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of SD1 and the application may be viewed on the web at http://www.ferc.gov using the 'eLibrary' link. Enter the project’s docket number, excluding the last three digits, in the docket number field to access the document. For assistance, contact FERC at FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov or call toll free, (866) 208-3676 or TTY (202) 502-8659.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the eLibrary docket-number search (exclude last three digits) and contact FERC Online Support for access help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Public Participation (OPP) assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s Office of Public Participation (OPP) supports meaningful public engagement and participation in Commission proceedings. OPP can help members of the public, including landowners, community organizations, Tribal members and others, access publicly available information and navigate Commission processes. For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, the public is encouraged to contact OPP at (202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPP is a resource for non-expert members of the public needing help understanding filing procedures or participating in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLibrary access to Combined Notice filings (docket query)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filings are accessible in the Commission’s eLibrary system by querying the docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To review rate filings and accessioned documents, search by docket number in eLibrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention/protest/answer filing rules (Rules 211, 214, 206) and party status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to intervene, to protest, or to answer a complaint in any of the above proceedings must file in accordance with Rules 211, 214, or 206 of the Commission’s Regulations (18 CFR 385.211, 385.214, or 385.206) on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern time on the specified comment date. Protests may be considered, but intervention is necessary to become a party to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review 18 CFR sections cited for procedural requirements. File timely and in the correct form to gain party status; protests alone do not confer party status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements reference and assistance contact
rubrics_metrics.description: eFiling is encouraged. More detailed information relating to filing requirements, interventions, protests, service, and qualifying facilities filings can be found at: http://www.ferc.gov/docs-filing/efiling/filing-req.pdf. For other information, call (866) 208-3676 (toll free). For TTY, call (202) 502-8659.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the linked filing-req.pdf for technical filing instructions and procedural details; contact FERC Online Support for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment date requirement for docketed filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each filing entry identifies a 'Comment Date' (for example, 'Comment Date: 5 p.m. ET 6/4/25'), which is the deadline for interested persons to submit comments relating to that filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor each docket's listed comment date; different dockets have different comment deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and requirements for submitting comments to FLRA OIG SORN
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before June 23, 2025. Submit comments identified by docket number OIG–2025–0001 via: (1) Federal eRulemaking Portal (https://www.regulations.gov), (2) Email: OIGMail@flra.gov, (3) Fax: (202) 208-4535, or (4) Mail: Federal Labor Relations Authority, Office of Inspector General, 1400 K Street NW, Floor 3, Washington, DC 20424. All submissions must include the agency name and docket number. All comments received will be posted without change to https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow docket identification instructions; be aware that comments are posted publicly without redaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLRA OIG system security classification
rubrics_metrics.description: FLRA OIG is modifying the security classification from 'Unclassified' to 'Sensitive but Unclassified and/or Controlled Unclassified Information' to more accurately reflect the sensitive nature of the records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records in this system are treated as SBU/CUI and handled consistent with those protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose(s) of FLRA OIG investigative system
rubrics_metrics.description: The records and information collected and maintained in this system are used to discharge the duties of the FLRA OIG, including: (a) receipt and/or investigation of allegations regarding a violation of any criminal or civil law, regulation, policy, or standard applicable to employees of the FLRA; (b) receipt and/or investigation of allegations regarding a violation of criminal or civil law, regulation, policy, standard, or contract having a nexus to the FLRA; and (c) to conduct inquiries and investigations into allegations of wrongdoing, whether criminal, civil, or administrative, made against FLRA employees, contractors, and other individuals or entities associated with the FLRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of collectable records and the legitimate uses for maintaining the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of individuals covered by the FLRA OIG system
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Subjects: individuals/entities against whom allegations have been made. 2. Complainants: individuals/entities alleging wrongdoing who may request anonymity/confidentiality. 3. Others: all other individuals/entities relevant to or contacted as part of an OIG matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories define whose information may be maintained and considered in the system; note separate handling for complainants and subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of records in the FLRA OIG system
rubrics_metrics.description: Records include letters, memoranda, complaints, correspondence relating to investigations, internal staff memoranda, subpoenas, affidavits, witness statements, transcripts, exhibits, documents obtained, interview notes, investigative notes, staff working papers, draft materials, opening/progress/closing reports, and other investigatory information or data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an inclusive list of investigatory records that may be collected and retained in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record source categories and retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Record Source Categories: See 'Categories of Individuals...above.' This system contains investigatory material for which sources need not be reported. Policies and Practices for Retrieval of Records: retrieval by the name of complainant or unique control number assigned to each complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrieval is keyed to complainant name or control number; investigatory sources may be withheld as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (a) — disclosure to investigative/implementing authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: To other agencies, offices, establishments, and authorities, whether Federal, State, Tribal, local, foreign, or self-regulatory (including professional associations or licensing boards), authorized or with responsibility to investigate, litigate, prosecute, enforce, or implement a statute, rule, regulation, or order, where the record indicates a violation or potential violation of law/contract or indicates a violation/potential violation of a professional, licensing, or similar regulation or reflects on qualifications/fitness of an individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows disclosure when records are relevant to investigations or enforcement by other authorities; includes Tribal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (b) — obtain information from private or governmental sources
rubrics_metrics.description: To any source, private or governmental, to the extent necessary to secure from such source information relevant to and sought in furtherance of a legitimate investigation or audit of the OIG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits outreach to third-party sources to gather information necessary for investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (c) — disclosures relevant to hiring/clearance/benefit actions
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Federal, State, Tribal, local, foreign, or self-regulatory agency or other public authority to the extent the information is relevant and necessary to the requestor’s hiring or retention of an individual or any other personnel action; issuance or revocation of a security clearance, license, grant, or other benefit; establishment of a claim; letting of a contract; reporting of an investigation of an individual; or for purposes of a suspension or debarment action, or initiation of administrative, civil, or criminal action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when records affect personnel decisions, security clearances, licensing, contracts, benefits, or enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (d) — disclosure to OPM/OGE/MSPB/OSC/EEOC
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Office of Personnel Management, the Office of Government Ethics, the Merit Systems Protection Board, the Office of Special Counsel, or the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, records or portions thereof relevant and necessary to carrying out their authorized functions (e.g., rendering advice requested by the OIG, investigations of alleged personnel practices, appeals, or authorized studies/reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports inter-agency collaboration on personnel, ethics, and merit-system matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (e) — disclosure to independent auditors/contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: To independent auditors or other private firms with which the OIG has contracted to carry out an independent audit or investigation, or to analyze/collate/aggregate or otherwise refine data collected in the system of records, subject to the requirement that such contractors shall maintain Privacy Act safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits sharing with contractors performing work for the OIG, provided Privacy Act safeguards are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (f) — disclosure in litigation or to DOJ for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: To the U.S. Department of Justice or in a proceeding before a court, administrative tribunal, or adjudicative body, when: (1) the FLRA; (2) OIG or any component thereof; (3) any employee of OIG in his/her official capacity; (4) any employee of OIG in his/her individual capacity where DOJ has agreed to represent the employee; or (5) the United States, where OIG determines that litigation is likely to affect FLRA or any of its components, is a party to the litigation or has an interest in such litigation, and OIG determines that use of such records is relevant and necessary to the litigation, provided OIG determines that disclosure is compatible with the purpose for which the records were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes disclosure of records to DOJ or in legal proceedings when relevant to defense/prosecution or representation matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (g) — disclosures to Members of Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Member of Congress from the record of a subject individual in response to an inquiry from the Member of Congress made at the request of that individual, but only to the extent that the record would be legally accessible to that individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits release to congressional offices responding to constituent inquiries, subject to legal access limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (h) — disclosure to direct recipients of Federal funds for corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: To any direct recipient of Federal funds, such as a contractor, where such record reflects serious inadequacies with a recipient’s personnel and disclosure of the record is for purposes of permitting a recipient to take corrective action beneficial to the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows sharing with funding recipients to enable corrective measures when personnel inadequacies are implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (i) — debt-collection contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: To debt-collection contractors for the purpose of collecting debts owed to the government as authorized by the Debt Collection Act of 1982, 31 U.S.C. 3718.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports debt collection activities using authorized contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (j) — breach response disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: To appropriate agencies, entities, and persons when (1) OIG or another component of the FLRA suspects or has confirmed that there has been a breach of the system of records; (2) OIG has determined that as a result of the suspected or confirmed breach there is a risk of harm to individuals, OIG or the FLRA, the Federal Government, or national security; and (3) the disclosure made to such agencies, entities, and persons is reasonably necessary to assist in connection with OIG’s or the FLRA’s efforts to respond to the suspected or confirmed breach or to prevent, minimize, or remedy such harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits targeted disclosure to respond to security incidents and mitigate harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (k) — disclosure to other Federal agencies to address breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: To another Federal agency or Federal entity, when the OIG determines that information from this system of records is reasonably necessary to assist the recipient agency or entity in (1) responding to a suspected or confirmed breach or (2) preventing, minimizing, or remedying the risk of harm to individuals, the recipient agency or entity, the Federal Government, or national security, resulting from a suspected or confirmed breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables interagency cooperation on breach response and remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (l) — disclosure to contractors/grantees/consultants/others working on government assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: To contractors, grantees, experts, consultants, students, and others performing or working on a contract, service, grant, cooperative agreement, or other assignment for the federal government, when necessary to accomplish an agency function related to this system of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows OIG to share records with external workers when needed to perform government functions, subject to privacy safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (m) — disclosure to DOJ for advice on OIG matters
rubrics_metrics.description: To the U.S. Department of Justice for the purpose of obtaining its advice on an OIG audit, investigation, or other inquiry, including Freedom of Information Act or Privacy Act matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits OIG to seek legal guidance from DOJ regarding investigations, FOIA, and Privacy Act issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (n) — disclosure to agencies/organizations for information relevant to OIG decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Federal, State, Tribal, local, or foreign agency, other public authority, law enforcement task force, consumer reporting agency, or professional organization maintaining civil, criminal, or other relevant enforcement or other pertinent records (such as current licenses), in order to obtain information relevant to an OIG decision concerning employee retention or other personnel action, issuance of a security clearance, letting of a contract or other procurement action, issuance of a benefit, establishment of a claim, collection of a delinquent debt, or initiation of an administrative, civil, or criminal action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain corroborating/licensing/enforcement records when making personnel, procurement, benefit, or enforcement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (o) — disclosure for computer matching and program integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Federal, State, Tribal, local, or foreign agency, other public authority, or law enforcement task force for use in computer matching to prevent and detect fraud and abuse in benefit or other programs administered by any agency, to support civil and criminal law enforcement activities of any agency and its components, and to collect debts and overpayments owed to any agency and its components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes use of records in automated cross-matching to detect fraud, abuse, and to collect debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (p) — disclosure for qualitative assessment/peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: To any official charged with the responsibility to conduct qualitative assessment, peer, or similar reviews of internal safeguards and management procedures employed in investigative, audit, inspection, and evaluation operations. This disclosure category includes members of the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE) or any successor entity and officials and administrative staff within their chain of command, as well as authorized officials of DOJ and the FBI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports oversight, peer review, and quality assessment of OIG operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (q) — disclosure to complainants/victims regarding progress/results
rubrics_metrics.description: To complainants and/or victims to the extent necessary to provide such persons with information and explanations concerning the progress and/or results of the investigation or case arising from the matters of which they complained and/or of which they were a victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits informing complainants/victims about investigation status and outcomes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (r) — disclosure to former OIG employees for official assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: To a former employee of OIG for purposes of: responding to an official inquiry by a Federal, State, Tribal, or local government entity or professional licensing authority, in accordance with applicable FLRA regulations; or facilitating communications with a former employee that may be necessary for personnel-related or other official purposes where OIG requires information and/or consultation assistance from the former employee regarding a matter within that person’s former area of official responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited disclosure to former employees when their assistance is necessary for official purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine use (s) — disclosure to NARA/OGIS for FOIA and records management purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: To the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), Office of Government Information Services (OGIS), to the extent necessary to fulfill its responsibilities under 5 U.S.C. 552(h), to review administrative agency policies, procedures, and compliance with FOIA, and to facilitate OGIS’ offering of mediation services to resolve disputes between persons making FOIA requests and administrative agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits sharing with archival and FOIA-oversight authorities for records management, FOIA compliance review, and mediation.
